settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC DOCK, NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC DOCK, NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: You're cold too.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: I'm a grown woman. I know how to be cold quietly. Come closer to the heater.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: We could move our bags.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: We could. Ask that woman if she'd like the end of the bench.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: Nine thousand residents depend on this berth's heating circuit. It wasn't closed for decoration.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: We voted to keep the gate sealed until they could isolate the fault. My parents live on that side of the ring.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I know what you voted for. What happened at the approach?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: An unscheduled freighter is coming in with the relief convoy. Somebody's shooting at it. They've got a couple hundred people aboard, maybe more.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: We do not have a couple hundred safe beds.

panelPlan: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC DOCK, NIGHT
He moves, but not far. A new group has arrived and he sees one of them eyeing the same warm space.
At the dock desk Wallace arrives with three residents who have been arguing over a heated berth they've paid to keep closed for maintenance. Jex is on a.

sourceActionBeats: *AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC DOCK, NIGHT*

*The warming room Halev opened is occupied. The family from Luminara is sleeping against one wall. The boy is awake and looks past the mother toward the only heater that seems to be winning against the room. In the civic dock office, Wallace has been called out of a meeting by a new alarm.*
*He moves, but not far. A new group has arrived and he sees one of them eyeing the same warm space.*

*At the dock desk Wallace arrives with three residents who have been arguing over a heated berth they've paid to keep closed for maintenance. Jex is on a communication line with a pilot. Halev looks at a distress feed.*
sourceScene: SCENE 1 — NO ROOM AT THE BERTH (RF_I02_P01)

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC DOCK, NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: No. I imagine that's why they didn't call ahead for a reservation.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Do we know who they are?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Verge families. Shard families. I don't know who's shooting. They're not sending a passenger list while someone cuts into the hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: If you open the gate, our circuit goes down again.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: It might. We'll move the sleeping families off that corridor first. I'll put the repair team at the breaker.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: And if my parents lose heat?

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then they come here, and you ask me why I didn't give them a better answer. I'm not going to tell you this is without cost.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The traders will withdraw their support.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: They'll get their chance to tell me so. Open the berth.

panelPlan: The resident studies the feed. Her anger has not vanished.
Outside, dockhands begin moving sleeping mats before the doors even finish cycling. The boy helps his mother fold a blanket for the newly arriving families. He.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The resident studies the feed. Her anger has not vanished.*

*Outside, dockhands begin moving sleeping mats before the doors even finish cycling. The boy helps his mother fold a blanket for the newly arriving families. He isn't heroic. The work is simply something he can do.*
sourceScene: SCENE 1 — NO ROOM AT THE BERTH (RF_I02_P01)

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD / EMPTY BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD / EMPTY BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: The latch won't hold by itself. Brace it there. No, not with your wrist. Use the bar. You won't have a wrist tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: There's a child on the other side who can't fit her mask.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: You need yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: She needs hers more.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: How long have we got?

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: In this section? Not long if the bridge keeps drinking the reserve. The pumps are feeding empty rooms.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Are you certain it's empty?

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Cameras and pressure sensors. I've checked every bridge compartment twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Then shut the bridge down.

panelPlan: MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD / EMPTY BRIDGE
Richard looks at the caregiver's own dwindling air reserve.
The caregiver moves before he can object. Richard watches the exchange, then calls to Paul.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD / EMPTY BRIDGE*

*The freighter is cramped, crowded, and practical. Richard Secundo is kneeling beside an adult holding a pressure panel with both hands. His nineteen-year-old son Paul works through the ship's physical service link on a repair slate. The empty bridge is still drawing power and atmosphere the passengers need.*
*Richard looks at the caregiver's own dwindling air reserve.*
*The caregiver moves before he can object. Richard watches the exchange, then calls to Paul.*

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD / EMPTY BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I'll lose half our instruments. And the helm station.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Which half do you need?

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I don't know yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Then work it out while we're breathing. Take the controls onto the slate.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: You keep saying that as if it's one switch.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: It usually isn't. If I could do it, I'd be on your side of the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: You'd make it worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Almost certainly.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Pressure's holding. But Dad—there's another noise. Something outside is making a hole.

panelPlan: Paul begins. His father's confidence is genuine, but it is also asking a lot of a nineteen-year-old.
The bridge starts going cold. The passenger section's pressure slows its decline. Something mechanical begins cutting through the outer skin.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Paul begins. His father's confidence is genuine, but it is also asking a lot of a nineteen-year-old.*
*The bridge starts going cold. The passenger section's pressure slows its decline. Something mechanical begins cutting through the outer skin.*

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD / EMPTY BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Then stay on the link. I'll take the breach.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: You can't fix a boarding cutter with a medical kit.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: No. But there'll be patients when it gets through.

panelPlan: They look at each other across the crowd. Then each goes where the other cannot.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *They look at each other across the crowd. Then each goes where the other cannot.*

settingText: ASHFANG MARAUDER — BOARDING GALLERY / SHARD CAPTAIN CHANNEL

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: ASHFANG MARAUDER — BOARDING GALLERY / SHARD CAPTAIN CHANNEL

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: That's a passenger ship. We agreed on cargo.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak won't move for cargo. It will move for people.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Billie, there are Shard families aboard. I know some of the names.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I know. And I know what Fleet let happen to ours. We're going to make Venn choose with everybody watching.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You don't know what she'll choose.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Then this should be educational.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAIDER
dialogueInline.text: The collar's on their passenger side. I can hear people through the skin.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Break off before you open it.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: The cargo will be ours once Thunderbreak leaves the screen. We're not here to shoot children.

panelPlan: ASHFANG MARAUDER — BOARDING GALLERY / SHARD CAPTAIN CHANNEL
Billie's crew is armed for a cargo seizure. The freighter ahead is not the cargo vessel they'd agreed to approach. Abby is on an independent.
One of Billie's boarders shifts uneasily.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *ASHFANG MARAUDER — BOARDING GALLERY / SHARD CAPTAIN CHANNEL*

*Billie's crew is armed for a cargo seizure. The freighter ahead is not the cargo vessel they'd agreed to approach. Abby is on an independent captain's channel; Tess is physically moving toward Gravefire's deployment link.*
*One of Billie's boarders shifts uneasily.*

settingText: ASHFANG MARAUDER — BOARDING GALLERY / SHARD CAPTAIN CHANNEL

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You've put children where you intend to threaten people. Do you not hear yourself?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I hear you defending a Fleet commodore you've never met.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I hear you doing something we didn't agree to. Change course.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Lock us on. Nobody leaves until Fleet answers.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You want Venn's attention? You've got mine. I'm bringing Gravefire to the breach.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Tess, don't start.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You started. And you're going to finish it without me on your hull.

panelPlan: Billie studies the two ship vectors. The opening she wants is almost within reach. She doesn't have the distance or the grace to admit she may have gone too.
The channel cuts. Billie is furious. Abby, on her own ship, orders her captains to hold civilian-clear vectors. Some comply. Billie still has ships willing to.

*The channel cuts. Billie is furious. Abby, on her own ship, orders her captains to hold civilian-clear vectors. Some comply. Billie still has ships willing to follow her.*

settingText: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND / NAOMI'S ESCORT / RESCUE ASSEMBLY

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND / NAOMI'S ESCORT / RESCUE ASSEMBLY

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION (comms)
dialogueInline.text: Your assignment is the supply screen. Remain there.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We have civilian registration data and a live distress transmission from Mercy of Dawn.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: And Shard docking codes. This could be a boarding trap. You are not authorized to expose Auric's essential cargo.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Turning now puts the medicine and heater freight outside our effective protection.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Dominion's order is on the command log.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: So is the distress call.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Do not turn Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Helm, take us to Mercy of Dawn. I'll answer for the diversion.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Auric, your convoy screen is gone. Pull what you can toward the port. We've got civilians in a damaged hull.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND / NAOMI'S ESCORT / RESCUE ASSEMBLY
The officer glances at her. He knows what she is about to do, and what it will cost her.
Naomi answers from her compact Verge escort.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *THUNDERBREAK COMMAND / NAOMI'S ESCORT / RESCUE ASSEMBLY*

*Auric's medicine and heating convoy needs protection. A different ship is transmitting live passenger distress. Dominion's authenticated order is already on the bridge. Venn's officers don't need to be taught what the competing duties mean.*
*The officer glances at her. He knows what she is about to do, and what it will cost her.*
*The turn begins. Venn speaks directly to Auric rather than waiting for a more comfortable phrasing.*
*Naomi answers from her compact Verge escort.*

settingText: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND / NAOMI'S ESCORT / RESCUE ASSEMBLY

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: We have a shuttle small enough for their service collar. My Second can keep the escort alongside while I board.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Fleet medics can launch with you. I'll have a security detail—

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Not with rifles at the front. Those people have already watched strangers cut through their hull. They'll think you're another boarding party.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: My officer has the engineering plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then let the officer handle the engineering. I'm the one who has to get through the passenger door without starting a panic.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Sol leads passenger contact. Fleet engineers follow. Rifles lowered. Officer, you're responsible for the structural approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I'll call when we have pressure.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Call sooner if you don't.

panelPlan: Venn looks at the feeds. She's angry about the loss of speed, but Naomi is right.
Naomi gives a short, involuntary laugh at an instruction so obviously impossible. She launches anyway. Venn remains responsible for a rescue she has chosen not.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn looks at the feeds. She's angry about the loss of speed, but Naomi is right.*
*Naomi gives a short, involuntary laugh at an instruction so obviously impossible. She launches anyway. Venn remains responsible for a rescue she has chosen not to control personally.*

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD / SERVICE SPINE HATCH

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD / SERVICE SPINE HATCH

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: We can fit the children and a caregiver, or some of the wounded. We cannot fit both groups intact.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Children first. We'll keep the rest breathing until we're back.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: Not without her.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: She gave me her air.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: She can't reach the shuttle alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then put her in my restraint. Carry her across.

dialogueInline.speaker: JUNIOR RESCUER
dialogueInline.text: That's your seat.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: It was. Fly the children. Don't make me argue with you about mathematics while the door is open.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Dad, the ship's opening at the joint. If the spine separates, I need to be on that side or I lose the helm.

panelPlan: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD / SERVICE SPINE HATCH
The child points at the Shard caregiver.
Across the compartment, Paul has discovered that the service-spine joint is failing. His control link runs through it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD / SERVICE SPINE HATCH*

*Only one rescue shuttle can load before the structure shifts again. The caregiver has given part of her air to a child; now both are too weak to stand. Naomi has to decide who takes the last seats. Richard knows exactly what will happen if the patients are separated carelessly.*
*The child points at the Shard caregiver.*

*The caregiver tries to protest. Naomi is already helping secure the harness. A nervous boy from another household helps keep the strap straight. The shuttle departs with the children and the caregiver. Naomi stays aboard with Richard and the adults.*
*Across the compartment, Paul has discovered that the service-spine joint is failing. His control link runs through it.*
sourceScene: SCENE 5 — THE PERSON YOU CAN CARRY (RF_I02_P06–P07)

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD / SERVICE SPINE HATCH

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Can you make it?

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: If I go now.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Clip your suit line. Tell me the instant you seal behind you.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I know the procedure.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: I know you do.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Leave the medicine.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAIDER
dialogueInline.text: Billie's order is to strip this hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Those cases are keeping patients breathing.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then they're staying. Move.

panelPlan: That lands more deeply than an order. Paul goes.
At the far cargo breach, a Shard raider is pulling medicine cases from a rack. Tess arrives, already exasperated by a fight she didn't want.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *That lands more deeply than an order. Paul goes.*
*At the far cargo breach, a Shard raider is pulling medicine cases from a rack. Tess arrives, already exasperated by a fight she didn't want.*
sourceScene: SCENE 5 — THE PERSON YOU CAN CARRY (RF_I02_P06–P07)

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD / SERVICE SPINE HATCH

dialogueInline.speaker: RAIDER
dialogueInline.text: You don't command this team.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You're right. I command the ship that can leave you here, and it's getting very difficult to remember why I shouldn't.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Hands where I can see them.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Yours too, if they're free. I need you to hold that pressure plate.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I'm not taking orders from a raider.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Lovely. We can die arguing over job titles. Or we can hold this plate shut.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Richard, get them behind the inner door.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: The hatch is bent. My slate won't fit through this gap.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'll clear it. Don't pull on the linkage, you'll shear the pins.

panelPlan: The raider hesitates. Naomi appears with a tool and sees a Shard officer facing another armed Shard.
Naomi moves to the plate. Air stops whistling through the bend. Tess's expression changes: the repair work is real, and Naomi knows what she's doing.
Paul reaches the spine access but cannot turn the distorted wheel.

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD / SERVICE SPINE HATCH

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: You sound like you've done this before.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Too often. And usually on ships belonging to Billie.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE (comms)
dialogueInline.text: You handed our supplies to Fleet.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I handed their medicine back. You can argue about it with me when the air stops leaking.

panelPlan: Tess frees the hatch. Paul squeezes through with his controls. The seal closes behind him. When Billie calls over the captain channel, Tess is at the far side.
Tess withdraws to Gravefire, while Naomi remains with Richard's passengers. No relationship has been repaired, but the immediate work holds.

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN / THUNDERBREAK / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / VEIL MARKET — INTERCUT AS ONE RESCUE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: MERCY OF DAWN / THUNDERBREAK / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / VEIL MARKET — INTERCUT AS ONE RESCUE

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Joint's gone. Tractor can hold either the passenger hull or the cargo spine.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI (comms)
dialogueInline.text: Three hundred people on this side. Pressure falling.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL (comms)
dialogueInline.text: I'm sealed in the spine. Helm still answers. Some of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Paul, I can't see you.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I can't see you either. I'm told it's very impressive out your window.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: This is not when you need to be funny.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: When would you prefer?

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV (comms)
dialogueInline.text: The supply spine carries heat and antibiotics for Auric. If we lose it, I have clinics rationing by morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know. Our tractor can't hold both.

panelPlan: MERCY OF DAWN / THUNDERBREAK / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / VEIL MARKET — INTERCUT AS ONE RESCUE
Richard almost answers, then the line rattles with an impact.
Venn looks at the passenger hull. There is no second tractor and no clever trick that conjures one.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *MERCY OF DAWN / THUNDERBREAK / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / VEIL MARKET — INTERCUT AS ONE RESCUE*

*The ship's structure finally fails. The passenger hull and supply spine separate. Paul is in the spine with the repair slate; Richard and Naomi are with the passengers. A single tractor hold from Thunderbreak can stabilize only one section at a time.*
*Richard almost answers, then the line rattles with an impact.*
*Venn looks at the passenger hull. There is no second tractor and no clever trick that conjures one.*

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN / THUNDERBREAK / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / VEIL MARKET — INTERCUT AS ONE RESCUE

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Hold the passengers. Keep Gravefire's approach open.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Understood. I'll protect the reserves we still have. Tell me honestly what reaches us.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: The spine still has a chance. You've used those bends before. We need the fixes.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Not on a public band. I built those routes for people who didn't want to be found.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Can you send them to Gravefire directly?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Their relay's gone. Half the ships out there don't hold the same private key. They've got a moving spine, no time, and not even a common map.

dialogueInline.speaker: SCRIBE
dialogueInline.text: If you give them only the first turn, they'll hit the shear at the second.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I know. That's why it isn't public.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Three safe houses use those approaches.

panelPlan: At Veil Market, Jex finds Halev's feed already waiting. The broker has a private route geometry the three factions cannot otherwise share in time.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *At Veil Market, Jex finds Halev's feed already waiting. The broker has a private route geometry the three factions cannot otherwise share in time.*

settingText: MERCY OF DAWN / THUNDERBREAK / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / VEIL MARKET — INTERCUT AS ONE RESCUE

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Three that I know about. There may be people who copied old routes because they thought nobody else would see them.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I won't order you to expose them.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: You don't have to. If that young man has no vector, he'll drift through a wreckage field until someone can write his name on a report.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Open all the fixes. Every anchor. Every timing window. Send word to the shelters that the route's burned.

dialogueInline.speaker: SCRIBE
dialogueInline.text: Both rescue vessels have it.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Good. I am going to need to make several very unpleasant calls.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Paul, nose toward the blue fracture. The slower edge, not the moving bright return.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS (comms, from Gravefire)
dialogueInline.text: Relative to you. Hold your orientation, I'll bring the reference around.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Paul, eyes on the slate.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I can't see your section.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: I'm here. You keep flying.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We won't fit through. Taking the outside course.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then go around. We can't wait for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Already turning.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Spine's slipping. I'll push from the side.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Your ship's already in pieces from the last raid.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: In very specific pieces. I know which ones can take another hit. Get Paul through.

settingText: SHATTERWAKE MOUTH / SHARD SKIFF CHANNELS / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERWAKE MOUTH / SHARD SKIFF CHANNELS / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Release the spine. There's a man inside it.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Tess comes aboard Ashfang. Then I let the cargo go.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You've already cut a passenger hull. I won't send Paul into another one.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You're making your choice public, Tess. You know that?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You've made nearly everything public today. I thought that was what you wanted.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: We were supposed to make Fleet answer for abandoning us. Now you're saving its cargo.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: There's a boy in that cargo. He happens to be nineteen, and he hasn't asked which side he belongs to before he tries to keep the engine running.

panelPlan: SHATTERWAKE MOUTH / SHARD SKIFF CHANNELS / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND
Billie catches the supply spine with a physical grapple. Paul is inside; the grapple pulls him off the vector Tess fought to give him. Abby sees the.
Billie is furious, mostly because Tess sounds disappointed rather than afraid.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *SHATTERWAKE MOUTH / SHARD SKIFF CHANNELS / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND*
*Billie catches the supply spine with a physical grapple. Paul is inside; the grapple pulls him off the vector Tess fought to give him. Abby sees the alignment and calls Billie.*
*Billie is furious, mostly because Tess sounds disappointed rather than afraid.*

settingText: SHATTERWAKE MOUTH / SHARD SKIFF CHANNELS / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Billie, listen. You have not put Venn where you think you have. You've put every Shard captain on that channel where they have to decide whether we threaten a boy to make a point.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Every captain can hear you defending Fleet.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They can hear me defending him. And they can hear you call that a crime.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Last chance. Move your skiffs.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Cut the grapple or I'll cut it for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Paul, hold the attitude jets steady. I've got your side.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Holding. I'm very interested in the part where we stop being attached to people who want to kill me.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Everyone aboard a ship eventually is. You are learning faster than most.

panelPlan: The silence lasts long enough for ships to move. A few skiffs pull toward Abby's civilian-clear line; others stay with Billie. None has been taken over by.
Billie's crew recovers its grapple and retreats with damage. She cannot bring herself to order fire through Tess. Abby's choices have protected.
Thunderbreak is approaching on the longer outside course. Billie's skiffs cross one firing solution as the tractor holds the passenger hull.

settingText: SHATTERWAKE MOUTH / SHARD SKIFF CHANNELS / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang in range. Clean shot for a moment.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Strike power would drop the tractor. The passengers go into debris.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Keep the tractor. Defensive drones only.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We could end the attack.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We could kill the people we're trying to rescue. No.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Incoming on our patched port armor.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Brace. Secure the bridge and keep pulling.

panelPlan: The ship shudders.
Gravefire steadies the spine. Cargo is damaged but not entirely lost. The passenger hull reaches safety. Nobody's agreement has been restored, and the.

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — ARRIVALS CONCOURSE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — ARRIVALS CONCOURSE

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: Shard arrivals stay behind the red barrier. That's what we were told.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: We're keeping care groups together until the medics have everyone assessed. A man with a lung injury doesn't become easier to treat because you make him cross the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: She gave me her air.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: Is anyone waiting for you?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: My sister was on the other shuttle. I can't find her.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: Use half our berth until you do. It's not generous. The room is too small and the heater makes an awful noise.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: We've got another blanket. It's mine, but you can have it.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: You were complaining that it's too scratchy.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: She can complain about it too.

panelPlan: AURIC BAZAAR — ARRIVALS CONCOURSE
The child the caregiver saved runs toward her. The caregiver tries to kneel and nearly collapses. The mother from Luminara catches her at the elbow.
The caregiver laughs once, which hurts. She accepts the blanket.

*Passengers emerge under medical supervision. The partial supply shipment comes in damaged. A civilian resident is trying to keep a newly erected faction barrier in place; an exhausted Shard caregiver from the first shuttle is still wearing the restraint that saved her life.*
*The child the caregiver saved runs toward her. The caregiver tries to kneel and nearly collapses. The mother from Luminara catches her at the elbow.*
*The caregiver laughs once, which hurts. She accepts the blanket.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — ARRIVALS CONCOURSE

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: We cannot fit everybody in those rooms.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: No, we cannot. Take down the unnecessary partitions. Medical triage by need. Housing assignments after.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You keep using words like temporary. When do the people who already live here get their space back?

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I have to answer that too. I can't answer it by separating a child from the woman who kept her alive.

panelPlan: The barrier comes down. Some residents help. Others stand aside, unconvinced, and their resentment doesn't evaporate into a neat lesson.

settingText: THUNDERBREAK — DAMAGED BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK — DAMAGED BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Hold Shard evacuees in Fleet custody. Request separate detention of the others at Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Auric is a civilian port. There are mixed households among our patients, including people who helped the evacuation.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: A security classification is not a penalty.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Separating patients from their carers will make it one. Some of the people you're classifying kept the children alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: We cannot ignore infiltration merely because a rescue was successful.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We don't have to ignore it. We can question people who are safe and medically able to answer. We can investigate the raiders without turning the passengers into prisoners.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK — DAMAGED BRIDGE
The rescued ships are moving toward a safe berth. Thunderbreak's tractor bus is overheated and the old port bow carries fresh damage over its earlier scrape..
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *THUNDERBREAK — DAMAGED BRIDGE*

*The rescued ships are moving toward a safe berth. Thunderbreak's tractor bus is overheated and the old port bow carries fresh damage over its earlier scrape. Dominion and Keating are on an authenticated Fleet link.*
sourceScene: SCENE 9 — WHAT GOES INTO THE LOG (RF_I02_P14)

settingText: THUNDERBREAK — DAMAGED BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Your ship was diverted against orders. Supply cargo was damaged. We have now had two incidents involving unauthorized Fleet decisions and Shard movement. I am not going to let a third become an administrative surprise.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: And I won't convert the civilian rescue into a detention operation.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Those were Naomi's rescue personnel, Admiral. They brought the children out.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: Officer, that's not your jurisdiction.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Comply, and Thunderbreak remains under your command.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I refuse the detention order. Record it without qualification.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Lieutenant Erin Deka will assume command as soon as the ship is safely berthed. Until then you're still responsible for her.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then I'll bring her to a safe berth and hand her over intact.

panelPlan: The ship's officer is working at an adjacent station, doing his best not to watch. He cannot remain silent when Dominion implies the rescue crews were.
Venn looks toward him—not reproachful, but a clear instruction to let her carry the consequence.
When the channel closes, the officer looks at Venn.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: You could have let me answer the first one.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: No. I couldn't.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: The ship has taken worse than this.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know. Let me know when the tractor bus has stopped arguing with engineering.

panelPlan: They return to work. Her command is ending, but not yet over.

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: These aren't abandoned apartments. Half the owners financed the work that made the ring possible. And the outer gallery is fractured.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: How much can we isolate from the glass?

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: These monitors still respond. But I'd want a second physical watch on the crack. I wouldn't trust the sensors alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: The patients can't keep moving between rooms. Some will not survive a second relocation tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The traders will argue that the cure is worse than the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: They're welcome to come and examine the problem. They can start by carrying a stretcher.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Inner rooms only. Every assignment recorded. The property claims remain intact. Find the owners and send them a notice they can actually answer.

panelPlan: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING
The Crown Ring is luminous, expensive and not empty. Some rooms belong to residents who are away; their belongings remain carefully stored. A.
Wallace starts to object, sees the exhausted staff, and decides against it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING*

*The Crown Ring is luminous, expensive and not empty. Some rooms belong to residents who are away; their belongings remain carefully stored. A monitored structural fracture has closed the outer gallery. Halev, Wallace, Richard and Paul inspect the safe inner section with the ring's own engineering staff.*
*Wallace starts to object, sees the exhausted staff, and decides against it.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The traders have already called a council vote.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Good. They can tell us what their alternative is. Meanwhile, repair crew at the isolation break, and two watches on the fracture. If it moves, everyone leaves.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: We may need to shift the heat load again.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: There isn't another spare circuit.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I said we may need to. I didn't say there was a cheerful answer.

panelPlan: Paul touches a cold frame and withdraws his hand.
Halev directs the first families into the secured inner area. A resident arriving with a key looks at them, at the door to her own apartment, and says nothing..

settingText: AURIC SERVICE AIRLOCK / CIVIC CHAMBER — CONTINUOUS POLITICAL AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC SERVICE AIRLOCK / CIVIC CHAMBER — CONTINUOUS POLITICAL AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You saved the passengers. We got some of the heaters back. Medicine too, enough to start an argument over who gets it first. My people still have to keep the ring warm.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I should have had a way to recover more of the spine.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You didn't. Don't turn it into a private apology. Tell me what your crews can leave us when you go.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: The emergency rescue stores are allocated for civilian use while this order stands. Your people can use them. Charts and engineering equipment, not tactical systems.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: And when Dominion changes his mind?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: My replacement can recall the Fleet personnel. I cannot promise relief beyond my authority.

panelPlan: AURIC SERVICE AIRLOCK / CIVIC CHAMBER — CONTINUOUS POLITICAL AFTERMATH
Naomi has finished a shift long enough to change the way she walks. Venn is still on Thunderbreak's side of the airlock for the last working handover. Neither.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC SERVICE AIRLOCK / CIVIC CHAMBER — CONTINUOUS POLITICAL AFTERMATH*

*Naomi has finished a shift long enough to change the way she walks. Venn is still on Thunderbreak's side of the airlock for the last working handover. Neither has had the luxury of being simply pleased about the rescue.*

settingText: AURIC SERVICE AIRLOCK / CIVIC CHAMBER — CONTINUOUS POLITICAL AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I don't want a Fleet base in exchange for a loan we didn't ask to need.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You won't get one from me. Verge remains responsible for civilian work.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then put the limit in writing. Halev needs to know precisely what disappears when they take you away.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I'll write what I can authorize.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That's useful. Not enough, but useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The traders have withdrawn their votes. The bonded stores stay locked.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: My parents' furniture is in that apartment. The books, their things. You can call it emergency use. I still want to know when they can go home.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Their claim stands. Nobody has transferred ownership.

panelPlan: Venn takes a moment. She knows Naomi has said 'they' rather than 'if'.
Elsewhere in the civic chamber, a resident holds an ownership claim while a Shard caregiver and her now-found sister wait by an open doorway. Wallace is giving.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn takes a moment. She knows Naomi has said 'they' rather than 'if'.*
*Elsewhere in the civic chamber, a resident holds an ownership claim while a Shard caregiver and her now-found sister wait by an open doorway. Wallace is giving Halev bad political news.*

settingText: AURIC SERVICE AIRLOCK / CIVIC CHAMBER — CONTINUOUS POLITICAL AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: My sister and I were told we'd get one night. If the vote closes the rooms, where do we go?

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You can use our kitchen. It's heated. The bedroom is still my parents'.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We'll find a place for both households. I can't promise it tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: We have recovered heaters for days, not a season. No replacement shipment confirmed. And you no longer have the votes to continue this order.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then publish the actual count. The order expires unless the council renews it. I'll answer them before it does.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You had better.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

panelPlan: The offer is not a political conversion. It is the limit of what this resident can bear to see happen tonight.
The resident finally looks at Halev rather than the apartment door.
Nothing in the room becomes simpler.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

*The resident finally looks at Halev rather than the apartment door.*

settingText: THUNDERBREAK — SECURED AURIC BERTH

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK — SECURED AURIC BERTH

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: The relief order is authenticated. Engineering has the inspection. I have the bridge when you're ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Port armor's compromised. Tractor bus is running hot. Two watches need replacing. You will find a stubborn valve that our crew has been threatening since the last refit.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Which valve?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You'll know it when you hear it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: You'd have made a better impression if you'd left me a whole bow.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I considered it. The raiders were inconsiderate about the approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I'll submit the repair orders. I don't intend to use the damage as an excuse to ignore the next convoy.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Nor should you. The ship's yours. My refusal and the rescue are both in the command log.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I can read.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK — SECURED AURIC BERTH
Thunderbreak is berthed at last. The tractor bus is still hot; port armor shows the new damage over the Kaldr scrape. Erin Deka arrives with the.
Deka checks the engineering report.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

settingText: THUNDERBREAK — SECURED AURIC BERTH

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: A comfort to hear from my successor.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I'll take care of her.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Auric directs civilian rescue. Verge escorts lead in Auric space. Shared emergency calls, access to the docks, review in thirty days.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: No permanent Fleet base. I'm signing for Auric, not the Admiralty.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: My skiffs can protect the civilian traffic. I can put the proposal to my captains. I cannot sign them into it.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: They follow civilian traffic control while they're in our approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I'll tell them. Each captain chooses.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: That's enough to begin. It is not enough to end the argument.

panelPlan: For a beat Deka's composure softens. She understands how much of Venn's life has been invested in this bridge.
The command changes hands with no invented ceremony. In the civic control room, a separate agreement is taking shape; it cannot be signed on behalf.
The agreement goes to the crews who will have to use it.

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING OBSERVATION GALLERY — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING OBSERVATION GALLERY — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Your fingers are still numb. Eat something.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: The ring watch is short of people.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: It will still be short of people after you eat. I'd prefer that to it being short of you.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I can do the late shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Wonderful. There is a compromise. I've only been suggesting it for an hour.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: They're flying my route without asking me now.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Are the safe houses moving?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The ones who can. One of the families is furious with me. Another sent thanks. I don't recommend either conversation.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Are you going to speak to them?

sourceActionBeats: *AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING OBSERVATION GALLERY — MORNING*

*This is not a victory montage. A partial cargo delivery is being sorted; one heating circuit remains isolated; a property dispute is being recorded by a tired civic clerk. People from different factions are eating a simple breakfast within sight of a station built for splendor.*
*Paul reaches for a repair kit. Richard stops his hand.*
*Across the room, Jex has been staring at new route copies pinned beside a working desk. Halev approaches.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING OBSERVATION GALLERY — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I suppose I should. It's an old habit, wanting the good part of a decision without meeting the people who got the bad part.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: The arrangement starts today. Fleet may still withdraw its limited rescue support.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then we'll have to build the rest ourselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: With people who may disagree with one another all day. We should be used to that.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: The tribunal has summoned me. I'll give them the complete log.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I know you will. I'm not sure it'll make them like you.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It doesn't have to.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: Are we staying here?

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: Tonight.

sourceActionBeats: *Naomi arrives with a working copy of the civilian compact.*
*Venn, no longer commander of Thunderbreak, passes the gallery on her way to Fleet transport. She stops only briefly. Naomi sees her.*
*Venn keeps walking. Her removal has not made her stop believing in Fleet, nor made the Verge's shortages disappear.*
*The boy from Luminara returns to the mother with the scratchy spare blanket folded under his arm.*
*The mother looks across the half-repaired room, where their luggage is still packed.*
*She takes the blanket and places it beside a stranger who is still cold.*
